AccountLimits.description: An account's effective caps in each mode: the operator's values over the defaults.

AccountPauseRequest.description: Administrative pause or resume of a whole account, in both modes.

example.reason: treasury on a sanctions list; review OPS-91

scopes.description: Pause scopes to add or remove: `quotes`, `settlement`, `refunds`.

AccountResponse.description: An account as the operator sees it.

api_keys.description:
The secret keys this request issued, each with its `secret` shown only here: at creation
a test key and, with `charges_enabled`, a live key; on an update that enables live mode,
the first live key. Send them to the contact; the merchant rolls them on receipt.

charges_enabled.description: Whether the account may use live mode.

max_unfinalized_credit.description:
Cap, in cents and per mode, on the credit of the account's deposits credited before they
are final; a deposit past it is credited once final.

restricted.description: Whether the account is restricted for review.

AdminReasonRequest.description: Administrative action body; `reason` is recorded in the action's audit row.

reason.description: Why the action is taken, 1 to 1024 bytes: the incident or sign-off it rests on.

AdminTreasuryPauseRequest.description: Administrative pause or resume of crediting to one treasury of an account.

example.reason: former treasury key reported compromised by the contact; OPS-97

reason.description: Why, for the audit log and the `treasury.updated` event's audit row.

ApiKeyObject.description: An API key (design D7). `secret` is present only in the response that created it.

expires_at.description: When a rolled key stops working, Unix seconds.

last_used.description: Last use, Unix seconds, to the minute.

permissions.description: A restricted key's permissions, such as `quotes.write`; `null` for a secret key.

redacted.description: The key's prefix and last four characters, such as `ppay_sk_test_…a1B2`.

secret.description: The whole key, `ppay_sk_…` or `ppay_rk_…`, shown once. Store it in a secret manager.

status.description:
`active`; `expiring` for a rolled key that still works until `expires_at`; `expired`;
`revoked`.

type.description: `secret`, holding every permission, or `restricted`, holding only `permissions`.

ChainRescan.description: One chain's rescan since the restore.

blocked.description:
Whether a reconciliation block freezes the chain: its scanner is paused, so it is left out
of the rescan, and it credits nothing until the block is lifted.

complete.description:
Whether the chain is rescanned: finalized past the moment the restore was detected, with
every issued address backfilled.

pending_backfills.description:
Issued addresses of the chain whose history the scanner has not read yet, such as
re-issued deposit addresses.

restored_block.description: The chain's scanned block when the restore was detected.

scanned_block_time.description: Block time of the finalized head the scanner last committed through, Unix seconds.

Contact.description:
The merchant's contact recorded at onboarding (design D8): the operator's channel for the key
hand-over, recovery, incidents, and restores, and the only personal data kept.

CreateAccountRequest.description: `POST /v1/admin/accounts` body. Accounts are created only by the operator (design D8).

charges_enabled.description: Whether the account may use live mode (design D12). Default `false`.

due_diligence.description: The due diligence the decision rests on.

reason.description: Why the account is created, 1 to 1024 bytes.

CustomerPauseRequest.description: Administrative pause or resume of one customer of an account.

livemode.description: The mode of the customer: customers of test and live mode are separate.

scopes.description: Pause scopes to add or remove.

DailyReportResponse.description: Daily finance report produced by C12.

exposure_minor.description:
Open rate-lock credit across all accounts in destination minor units: the sum the global
exposure cap is enforced against. This service always sends it; it is optional in the
schema so clients also parse reports from servers that predate it.

failing_webhook_endpoints.description:
Enabled webhook endpoints of any account whose oldest undelivered event is older than
`failing_for_hours`, oldest first. Deliveries are retried until delivered and never given
up on, so each has failed that long; contact the account (docs/integration.md,
"Delivery health").

oneOf.description:
Latest reconciliation round of the serving process; absent until the first round after a
restart.

routes.description: SQL-computed metrics for each configured route.

DeliveredEventFinding.description: An imported event whose deposit is not re-derived yet, or whose amounts differ.

delivered_amount.description: Delivered `amount`, the credit in minor units.

ledger_amount.description: The ledger's credit in minor units.

status.description:
`pending` (the rescan has not re-derived or valued the deposit yet) or `mismatch` (the
ledger's token amount or credit differs from what the merchant received; the delivered
event is kept and never sent again).

DeliveredEvents.description: Delivered events imported for the restore.

findings.description: Each imported event whose deposit the ledger does not hold as delivered yet.

Deposit.description:
A transfer to a quote's address or a deposit address at the route's confirmation: valued,
screened, and credited, or rejected; `reversed` if its transaction left the chain before
finality.

Every `deposit.*` event carries the whole deposit, with cumulative amounts, so the customer's
balance can be recomputed from the latest snapshot whatever order events arrive in: the
deposit contributes `amount - amount_refunded - amount_reversed` cents while its `status` is
`credited` or `reversed`, and nothing while it is `pending` or `rejected`. `status` only moves
forward (`pending`, then `credited` or `rejected`, then possibly `reversed`) and
`amount_refunded` only grows, so of two snapshots the later one has the later status or, for
the same status, the larger `amount_refunded`.

oneOf.description: The operator's view of the deposit's internals; only in `GET /v1/admin/deposits/{id}`.

amount.description: Credit in the currency's minor unit (cents), once valued.

amount_atomic.description: Token amount in base units, as a decimal string.

amount_refunded.description:
Cents of `amount` its succeeded refunds take back: `amount` times `amount_refunded_atomic`
over `amount_atomic`, rounded down, so it never exceeds the refunded share, and all of
`amount` once fully refunded. Computed from the cumulative refunded amount, it only grows.
`0` without `amount`.

amount_refunded_atomic.description: Refunded token amount in base units, as a decimal string: the sum of succeeded refunds.

amount_reversed.description:
Cents of `amount` the reversal takes back: `amount` once `status` is `reversed` (a
deposit is refunded only once final, and a final deposit is never reversed, so a reversed
deposit has no refunds); `0` otherwise.

asset.description: Asset code; `null` for a token without a route.

block_number.description: Number of the block the transfer is in; it changes if the transaction is re-included.

client_reference_id.description: Your identifier of the customer the deposit is credited to.

deposit_address.description:
The deposit address that received the transfer, `da_…`, on `chain_id` at `address`; `null`
for a quote's address. Payments to a deposit address, active or retired, are credited at
spot.

exchange_rate.description: USD per token, a decimal string with 8 places, once valued.

final.description:
Whether the deposit's block is final on both providers: a final deposit can no longer be
reversed, and only a final deposit can be refunded. A deposit is credited at the route's
confirmation, before it is final (`GET /v1/config` `typical_finality_seconds`).

final_at.description:
When the finality watch found the deposit's block final on both providers, Unix seconds;
`null` until `final`.

id.description:
`dep_` and the hex of the deposit's deterministic UUID,
`uuid_v5(DEPOSIT_NAMESPACE, "{chain_id}:{tx_hash}:{receipt_log_index}")`, where
`receipt_log_index` is the transfer's position among its transaction's receipt logs. A
deposit recorded at a position after `revision` earlier deposits there were reversed (a
re-included transaction that paid differently) appends `:{revision}` to the name.

livemode.description: Whether the deposit is on a live-mode route.

log_index.description: Block-wide log index of the transfer; it changes if the transaction is re-included.

metadata.description:
Your key/value pairs ([metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata)): a copy of the
quote's or the deposit address's when the deposit is recorded, independent of it
afterwards; `{}` when none.

oneOf.description: The quote whose address received the transfer; `null` for a deposit address.

refunded.description: Whether the deposit is fully refunded.

rejection_reason.description:
Why the deposit was rejected: `unsupported_asset`, `below_minimum`, `out_of_bounds`,
`out_of_range`, or `sanctioned`.

status.description:
`pending` (recorded at the route's confirmation and being valued and screened, or held
while the account's or customer's `settlement` is paused), `credited`, `rejected` (see
`rejection_reason`), or `reversed` (its transaction is not in the final chain: its credit is
taken back, `amount_reversed`). New values may be added.

swept.description:
Whether a finalized `Flushed` event after the deposit moved its forwarder's balance of
its token to the treasury (`GET /v1/sweeps`), whoever sent the flush.

DepositAddress.description:
A customer's persistent deposit address, like a bank-transfer virtual account: one address for
every supported token on every supported network. Any amount of a supported token sent to it
is credited to the customer at the market (spot) price when it arrives. Rotation retires it and
issues a new one on every network; a retired address is still credited.

address.description:
The address shared by every network, when all of `networks` have the same one; `null`
when a network's treasury differs, and so its address (see `networks`), or when there is
no network.

client_secret.description:
Lets the customer's page read the address's public view, `ClientDepositAddress`, from
`GET /v1/deposit_addresses/{id}?client_secret=…` without an API key, to show a payment as
soon as it is seen. Returned only by `POST /v1/deposit_addresses` and `…/rotate`, each
time a new one; only its hash is stored, and the newest 10 of an address stay valid. Give
it only to the customer's page, and do not log it.

livemode.description: Whether the address is in live mode.

metadata.description:
Your key/value pairs ([metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata)); `{}` when none.
Each deposit to the address starts with a copy.

networks.description:
The address on each supported network of the mode it was issued on, by `chain_id`, with
the tokens it takes there.

payments.description:
Payments to the address in the last 24 hours, newest first, at most 10, as a quote's
`payment`: `seen` in a block within about a block time of arriving, then `recorded` as a
deposit. Display only; credit from `deposit.credited`.

retired_at.description: Retirement time, Unix seconds; `null` while active.

salt.description: CREATE2 salt, 32 bytes of hex; the same on every network.

status.description: `active`, or `retired` by a rotation; payments to either are credited.

version.description:
The address's version among the customer's addresses, from 1. The salt is
`keccak256(abi.encode(account, livemode, client_reference_id, "deposit_address", version))`,
with the types `(string, bool, string, string, uint256)` and `account` your `acct_` id; it
names no chain or asset. On each network the address is the factory's `CREATE2` over that
network's treasury and the salt.

DepositAddressAsset.description: A token a deposit address takes on one network.

payment_uri.description:
EIP-681 ERC-20 transfer URI carrying the token, chain, and address, and no amount: the
payer chooses it.

DepositAddressNetwork.description: A deposit address on one network (EVM chain).

address.description: The forwarder address to pay on this chain.

assets.description: The supported tokens on this chain; any other token sent to the address is not credited.

treasury.description:
The treasury the forwarder pays. The address is the same on every network whose treasury
is the same address.

DepositAdmin.description:
The operator's view of a deposit's internals (`GET /v1/admin/deposits/{id}`), returned as the
`admin` field of the deposit; never present in a merchant response or an event.

account.description: The merchant account the deposit belongs to, `acct_…`.

events.description: Events about the deposit in ascending creation order, with their delivery.

final_at.description: When both providers showed the transfer at or below `finalized`.

price_scaled.description: Eight-decimal scaled price as a decimal string.

receipt_log_index.description:
Position of the transfer log in its transaction's receipt; with the chain and transaction,
the deposit's identity.

state.description:
The processing state: `detected`, `confirmed`, `credited`, `swept`, `rejected`, or
`reversed` (`status` is its merchant view).

DepositEventDelivery.description: An event about a deposit and its delivery state.

delivered_at.description:
When the last of the account's webhook endpoints accepted the event, or `null` while one
has not or the account has none.

DepositTransition.description: One immutable state transition of a deposit.

attempt.description: Retry attempt recorded for this transition.

DueDiligence.description:
The record of the operator's offline due diligence (design D8): a reference to it, when, and
by whom.

reference.description: Reference to the review in Phala's records, 1 to 200 characters.

ErrorDetail.description: Stable error fields safe to expose to callers.

message.description: Human-readable summary without internal details; it may change.

param.description: The request parameter the error is about, when there is one.

type.description:
Error category: `invalid_request_error` for any 4xx except an idempotency conflict,
`idempotency_error` for an `Idempotency-Key` reused with another request or still in use,
`api_error` for 5xx.

ErrorResponse.description:
Machine-readable error envelope returned by every API failure, Stripe's error object
(<https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors>).

error.message: the deposit is not final yet; request the refund once it is (about 15 minutes after its block on Ethereum)

EventImport.description: What importing one delivered event did.

result.description:
`imported` (stored as delivered, with no delivery), `matches` (recorded already with the
same `data`), or `mismatch` (recorded already with other `data`, which is kept).

ExpandableQuote.description: A quote id, or the quote with `expand[]`.

FailedCheckReport.description: One reconciliation check that could not complete.

error.description: Error that stopped the check, without provider URLs.

FailingWebhookEndpoint.description: A webhook endpoint failing for longer than the daily report's threshold.

last_attempt_status.description: That attempt's HTTP status; `null` when no response arrived.

oldest_pending_at.description: Creation time of its oldest undelivered event.

pending_deliveries.description: Deliveries to it not delivered yet.

example.name: recovery
example.reason: contact verified by phone after a lost key, ticket OPS-88

name.description: The key's label, at most 200 characters.

reason.description: Why, 1 to 1024 bytes: how the request was verified with the recorded contact.

revoke_existing.description: Revokes every key of the mode first, for a leak the merchant cannot win by rolling.

Limits.description: The caps of one account in one mode.

max_active_deposit_addresses.description: Active deposit addresses the account may hold in the mode.

max_open_amount_per_account.description: Cap on the credit of the account's open quotes in the mode, in cents.

max_open_amount_per_customer.description: Cap on the credit of one customer's open quotes, in cents.

max_open_quotes.description: Open quotes the account may hold in the mode.

scopes.description: Pause scopes to add or remove.

PauseResponse.description: Current scopes after a pause mutation.

Payment.description:
A payment observed at a quote's address or a deposit address. Display only: while `status` is
`seen` it may still disappear in a reorg, and nothing has been credited.

amount_atomic.description: Token amount in base units, as a decimal string.

asset.description: Asset code; `null` for a token without a route.

confirmations.description: Blocks on top of and including the transfer's block at the last head scan; `seen` only.

deposit.description: `dep_` id the deposit has, or will have once recorded.

estimated_final_at.description: Estimated finality time, Unix seconds: block time plus 15 minutes; `seen` only.

matches_quote.description:
On a quote: whether the payment is the quote's asset, in time, and within tolerance, so
it is credited at the quoted price (otherwise at spot). `null` on a deposit address, whose
payments are all credited at spot.

status.description:
`seen` (in a block, not recorded as a deposit yet) or `recorded` (recorded as a deposit at
the route's confirmation; follow it as `deposit`). New values may be added.

ReceivedTreasury.description: A treasury object as the merchant received it; other fields are ignored.

crediting_paused_by.description:
The received `crediting_paused_by`; only its `merchant` entry is compared, the operator
re-applies its own pauses.

lifted_at.description: When the block was lifted; a repeated lift returns the original time.

check.description: Check that wrote the block, such as `address_derivation`.

scope.description:
`chain`: the chain is frozen. No check writes the `address` scope any more; it excluded an
address from the removed operator flusher.

ReconciliationRoundReport.description: Latest reconciliation round of the serving process.

failed_checks.description: Checks that could not complete; empty after a complete round.

RestoreApiKeyRevokeRequest.description:
`POST /v1/admin/restore/api_keys/revoke` body: a key the merchant revoked after the restore
point, named by its id or by its prefix and last four characters.

example.reason: revoked by the merchant at 10:02 PDT, after the restore point; INC-12

last4.description: The key's last four characters, with `prefix`.

prefix.description: The key's prefix, such as `ppay_sk_live_`, with `last4`.

reason.description: Why, 1 to 1024 bytes: the merchant's record of the revocation.

RestoreDepositAddressRequest.description:
`POST /v1/admin/restore/deposit_addresses` body: a deposit address the merchant holds, given
out after the restore point.

example.reason: issued after the restore point, from the merchant's records; INC-12

address.description:
The address the merchant holds (the top-level `address` or a network's); the version is
found by deriving the customer's versions over the account's current treasuries.

id.description: The `da_` id the merchant holds, kept for the re-issued address.

version.description: The address's `version`; with `address`, both must agree.

reissued.description: Whether the address was issued now; `false` when the customer already had this version.

RestoreEventsImportRequest.description:
`POST /v1/admin/restore/events` body: `deposit.credited`, `deposit.rejected`, and
`deposit.reversed` events the merchant received after the restore point, as delivered.

example.reason: delivered after the restore point, from the merchant's receiver; INC-12

events.description: Up to 100 event objects exactly as delivered.

data.description: One result per event, in request order.

RestoreObject.description: A restore from backup the service detected.

detected_at.description: When the service found the restore and froze, Unix seconds.

detected_by.description:
`restore_check` (recorded after a restore on boot of the restore-check variant) or
`timeline` (`topup run` found a PostgreSQL timeline newer than the acknowledged one).

restore_point.description: Newest heartbeat in the restored database, Unix seconds: changes after it may be lost.

restored_cursors.description:
Each chain's scanned block when the restore was detected, by chain id: where the rescan
starts, and where a re-issued deposit address is backfilled from.

timeline_id.description: The PostgreSQL timeline the restore promoted to.

unfrozen_at.description: When the operator unfroze the service, Unix seconds.

RestoreStatus.description:
`GET /v1/admin/restore`: the restore freeze and the reconciliation before unfreezing
(`deploy/RESTORE.md`).

delivered_events.description: Delivered events imported from merchants' records, compared with the ledger.

frozen.description:
Whether the service is frozen after a restore from backup: merchant writes answer
`503 service_restoring`, and nothing credits, settles, expires a quote, applies a treasury
change, verifies a refund, or delivers an event.

rescan.description:
The rescan of each configured chain since that restore; the freeze lifts only once every
chain is `complete`.

oneOf.description: The most recent restore; `null` when the database was never restored.

RestoreTreasuryVerifyRequest.description:
`POST /v1/admin/restore/treasuries/verify` body: the treasuries of the merchant's latest
`treasury` events, as received.

example.reason: the merchant's treasury events since the restore point; INC-12

reapply.description:
Apply again what the restore undid: cancel each pending treasury the merchant received as
`canceled`, and pause or resume crediting as the merchant's `crediting_paused_by` shows.

treasuries.description:
Each treasury's latest object the merchant received (an event's `data.object`), one per
treasury; at most 100.

data.description: One result per received treasury, in request order.

RestoreUnfreezeRequest.description: `POST /v1/admin/restore/unfreeze` body: the operator's reason and checklist.

example.reason: INC-12 reconciled with every merchant; signed off by the on-call lead

delivered_events_imported.description: Every event delivered after the restore point was imported; must be `true`.

deposit_addresses_reissued.description: Every deposit address given out after the restore point was re-issued; must be `true`.

reason.description: Why, 1 to 1024 bytes: the incident and its sign-off.

security_changes_reapplied.description:
Every contact confirmed the key revocations, treasury cancellations, and endpoint
deletions made after the restore point, and each was applied again; must be `true`.

RestoreWebhookEndpointDeleteRequest.description:
`POST /v1/admin/restore/webhook_endpoints/delete` body: an endpoint the merchant deleted
after the restore point.

example.reason: deleted by the merchant after the restore point; INC-12

RouteDailyReport.description: Per-route daily finance report produced by C12.

age_in_state_max_seconds.description: Maximum age in seconds keyed by current deposit state.

credited_undelivered.description: Credited deposits whose `deposit.credited` webhook an endpoint has not acknowledged yet.

credited_undelivered_max_age_seconds.description: Age in seconds of the oldest of those events; zero when every one was delivered.

open_rate_lock_exposure_atomic.description: Sum of unconsumed rate-lock token amounts.

rejected_holds_atomic.description: Rejected token amount still held after succeeded refunds.

unflushed_balance_atomic.description:
Deposits not reversed minus finalized `Flushed` amounts: what the route's forwarders
still hold for their merchants to sweep.

Treasury.description:
An account's treasury of one chain and mode (design D10): the only address the forwarders
issued over it can pay.

canceled_at.description: When it was canceled, Unix seconds.

cancellation_reason.description:
Why it was canceled: `requested` (you canceled it) or `sanctioned` (a sanctions list named
the address when the change was due to apply, so it never applied).

created.description: When it was proven, Unix seconds.

crediting_paused.description:
Whether crediting of deposits to forwarders over this address is paused: they stay
`pending` and no `deposit.credited` is sent until it resumes.

crediting_paused_by.description:
Who paused crediting: `merchant` (`POST /v1/treasuries/{id}/pause`) and, or, `operator`.
Each lifts only its own pause.

effective_at.description:
When the treasury applies or applied, Unix seconds: at once for a chain's first treasury
and in test mode, 48 hours after the proof for a later live change.

kind.description:
`eoa` (an EIP-191 signature recovered to the address) or `contract` (a deployed
contract's EIP-1271 approval).

replaced_at.description: When a later treasury replaced it, Unix seconds.

status.description:
`pending` (a live change waiting for `effective_at`; cancel it with
`POST /v1/treasuries/{id}/cancel`), `active` (the chain's current treasury: new quotes and
deposit address networks pay it), `replaced` (a former treasury; addresses issued over it
still pay it), or `canceled`.

TreasuryVerification.description: A received treasury compared with the restored one.

result.description:
`matches`; `canceled` (canceled again now); `cancellation_lost` (the merchant canceled it,
the restore undid it: cancel it with `reapply`); `missing` (created after the
restore point: the merchant creates it again after the unfreeze); or `differs` (another
status, chain, or address; a change that applied after the restore point applies again).

status.description: The restored treasury's status now; `null` when it is missing.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: `POST /v1/admin/accounts/{account}` body; absent fields stay as they are.

example.reason: live mode approved after legal sign-off

charges_enabled.description:
Enables or disables live mode. Enabling it for an account without a live key returns the
account's first live key.

oneOf.description: Changes the account's caps in one mode (design §12); absent caps stay.

max_unfinalized_credit.description:
Sets the cap, in cents and per mode, on the credit of the account's deposits credited
before they are final: a deposit whose credit would take that total past it is credited
once final instead. Default 100 000 ($1 000); `0` credits every deposit at finality.

restricted.description: Marks the account restricted for review.

UpdateLimitsRequest.description: The caps of one mode an operator changes; absent fields stay.

livemode.description: The mode whose caps change: test mode's caps never limit live mode, nor the reverse.

max_active_deposit_addresses.description: Active deposit addresses the account may hold in the mode, at least 1.

max_open_amount_per_account.description: Cap on the credit of the account's open quotes in the mode, in cents.

max_open_amount_per_customer.description: Cap on the credit of one customer's open quotes, in cents.

max_open_quotes.description: Open quotes the account may hold in the mode, at least 1.

http_message_signature.description: An RFC 9421 ed25519 signature over `@method`, `@target-uri`, `content-digest`, and `idempotency-key` when sent. `@target-uri` is the service's configured public origin (`TOPUP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`) followed by the request path and query, so sign the public URL you call; `Host` and `X-Forwarded-*` headers are ignored.
http_message_signature.name: Signature

info.description: The operator's API (design D8): accounts, recovery keys, pauses, and platform health. Every request is signed with the operator's RFC 9421 key; merchants never call it. The merchant API is `openapi.json`.
info.title: Phala Pay admin API

200.description: OK: created, with its first secret keys

409.description: `idempotency_key_in_use`: a request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running; retry with the same key

post.summary:
Creates a merchant account after the operator's offline due diligence (design D8): records the
contact and the due diligence, decides live mode (`charges_enabled`, D12), and returns the
first secret key of test mode and, with live mode, of live mode. Each key's `secret` is shown
only in this response; send it to the contact, who rolls it on receipt. Audited.

200.description: OK: updated, or already holding these values

404.description: Not Found: no account has this id

409.description: `idempotency_key_in_use`: a request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running; retry with the same key

post.summary:
Updates an account: live mode (enabling it returns the first live key), the restricted flag,
the contact, the cap on credit before finality, or the caps of one mode (`limits`). Audited, and announced to the account as `account.updated`. The operator does
not manage the account's webhook endpoints: the merchant does, with `/v1/webhook_endpoints`.

200.description: OK: the key with its `secret`, shown once

403.description: `testmode_charges_only`: a live key for an account without live mode

404.description: Not Found: no account has this id

409.description: `idempotency_key_in_use`: a request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running; retry with the same key

post.summary:
Issues a recovery key (design D7) after the operator verified the request with the recorded
contact, optionally revoking every key of the mode first. Audited, and announced as
`api_key.*` events with actor `admin`.

announced as `treasury.updated`.

Re-issues a deposit address the merchant gave a customer after the restore point, from the
merchant's record of its address or version: the salt is derived from the account, mode,
customer, and version, so it is the same address, backfilled from the restored cursor so the
rescan credits payments made to it since. Audited.

post.summary:
Imports the deposit events a merchant received after the restore point, exactly as delivered:
each is stored as the event it is, with no delivery, so when the rescan re-derives the deposit
its event is recorded already and nothing is sent again with another body. An event recorded
already keeps its stored snapshot; a different delivered body is reported as `mismatch`.
Audited.

post.summary:
Compares the treasuries of the merchant's latest `treasury` events with the restored ones and,
with `reapply`, cancels again each pending change the merchant canceled after the restore point
(while frozen no treasury change applies, so none takes effect first) and pauses or resumes
crediting again as the merchant last did. Audited, each change announced as `treasury.*`.

event delivery resume, and merchants can write again. The reason and checklist are recorded
in the restore and in `audit`.
